short_bio: American novelist and winner of the 1993 Nobel Prize in Literature.
biography:
Toni Morrison was born Chloe Ardelia Wofford in Lorain, Ohio, and studied at Howard University and Cornell. She worked as an editor at Random House while writing, and published her first novel, The Bluest Eye, in 1970.

Song of Solomon (1977) won the National Book Critics Circle Award, and Beloved (1987) won the 1988 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. In 1993 she became the first Black woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012 and died on 5 August 2019.
